title: Exit Ticket: Adding Fractions
subject: math
instructions: Write your ID number in the boxes, not your name. Show your work.

questions.prompt: Strip Sum: The top strip shows 1/3 and the middle strip shows 1/4. Shade the bottom strip to show 1/3 + 1/4. Then write the sum.

diagram.description: Three fraction strips of the same length, stacked. Top strip: 3 equal parts with 1 shaded, labeled 1/3 on the left. Middle strip: 4 equal parts with 1 shaded, labeled 1/4 on the left. Bottom strip: 12 equal parts with none shaded, labeled 1/3 + 1/4 on the left, and '= ________' printed to its right for the sum.

checklist.item: Exactly 7 of the 12 parts in the bottom strip are shaded (usually 4 for 1/3, then 3 for 1/4).
The sum written after the = sign is 7/12.

questions.prompt: Walk to the Library: Rosa walks 1/2 mile to the park. Then she walks 3/5 mile to the library. How far does she walk in all?
questions.key: Rewrites both fractions with a common denominator of 10 (5/10 + 6/10) and adds to get 11/10, which is 1 1/10 miles. 11/10 or 1 1/10 is full credit. The mistake to look for: adding the tops and the bottoms to get 4/7.

questions.prompt: Spot the Sum: Which one equals 1/2 + 1/3? Circle the letter.

options.why: That adds tops and bottoms. 2/5 is less than 1/2, so it's too small.
Yes: 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6, so the sum is 5/6.
Sixths plus sixths are still sixths. Keep 6 as the denominator.
